<think>The user asks: "Recomienda tres libros sobre aprendizaje automático adecuados para un lector de nivel intermedio. Cada entrada: title, author, year, why_recommended."

They want a JSON object with three entries, each containing fields: title, author, year, why_recommended. Probably they want a list of objects.

The system says: "Solo produce un objeto JSON válido — sin prosa, sin markdown."

Thus we must output a JSON object, not markdown code fences, no extra text. Must be valid JSON.

The JSON could be an array of objects. Each object has title (string), author (string), year (number), why_recommended (string). Provide three books.

Potential books for intermediate machine learning:

- "Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow" by Aurélien Géron (2nd edition 2019) or 3rd edition 2022. Year maybe 2019 (2nd) or 2022 (3rd). Provide whichever.

- "Machine Learning Yearning" by Andrew Ng (not a typical textbook but technical). But maybe "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" by Christopher Bishop (2006). But that might be more advanced. But intermediate? Could be okay.

- "Deep Learning" by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville (2016). That's advanced but could be intermediate.

- "Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading" by Stefan Jansen (2020) but maybe not.

- "Machine Learning Engineering" by Andriy Burkov (2020). Good for intermediate.

- "The Elements of Statistical Learning" by Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman (2009). That is more advanced but can be intermediate.

- "Fundamentals of Machine Learning for Predictive Data Analytics" by John D. Kelleher, Brian Mac Namee, Ao
